A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FAN: Fourier Analysis Networks. Their complete main text and Appendices A–D are readable, and equations, figures, tables and experiments can be matched across the appendix additions and layout changes.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 and the appendices report original function-fitting, time-series forecasting and sentiment-analysis experiments, including comparisons with other networks.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds image-recognition/OOD experiments and forecasting results with instance normalization in Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: FAN's layer definition, stacking, gating and MLP-replacement procedure are retained. Equation 11 adds explicit layer indices, and Figure 2 corrects connections to match the existing definition. The CNN experiment applies the same replacement procedure.

E1.justification: Table 4 adds image classification on MNIST, MNIST-M, Fashion-MNIST and Fashion-MNIST-C, including paired OOD evaluation. Table 5 separately identifies ETTh1 and ETTh2, whereas the retained Table 2 labels only ETTh; the exact ETT coverage expansion is therefore unclear.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds a CNN baseline against CNN with FAN. The additional normalized forecasting comparison includes Transformer and its two FAN variants, without LSTM or Mamba; both remain in the original Table 2 comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds an instance-normalized forecasting setting and an image-evaluation protocol reporting best-epoch, final-epoch and paired OOD accuracy. Appendix C.5 specifies 100 epochs of SGD with momentum and learning rate 0.01 for image recognition. The previously reported protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds paired-domain and corruption-transfer tests for image recognition, plus forecasting experiments examining performance with instance normalization. These substantially extend checks of generalization and preprocessing dependence. Existing periodicity, training-curve and Snake analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables continue reporting point estimates; best-epoch and final-epoch accuracies do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 4–5 add substantial results under new settings. Image outcomes are mixed: the MNIST row reports final OOD accuracy of 22.12 for CNN versus 21.64 with FAN. Normalized forecasting reports average MSE of 0.554 for Transformer, 0.526 with gated FAN and 0.509 with default FAN. Original result figures and Tables 2–3 retain their values.

T1.justification: The Fourier-series derivation, mathematical definitions and expressive-power argument remain substantively unchanged. Equation 11 makes layer indices explicit without adding or revising a theorem, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about periodicity modeling, generalization, MLP replacement and reduced parameters/FLOPs. The appendix experiments add supporting evidence without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of periodicity, generalization and applicability remain unchanged, with no new substantive limitations or mechanism arguments. Table 5's statement that normalization improves performance is an added empirical observation.

D1.justification: Appendix C.5 newly describes the CNN's four convolutional and two MLP layers, replacement with FAN, approximate parameter matching, optimizer, learning rate and training duration. Existing implementation descriptions and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, identifiable cited works and positioning relative to earlier periodic-activation and Fourier-network approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to new appendix captions and subsection C.5, explicit layer indices in Equation 11, and small wording edits. Section 4.1 introduces the typo 'modelingy'; the main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–5, reflows the appendices and resizes Figure 7. Figure 2 corrects the cosine/sine connections to share projected features consistently with Equation 9. Existing result figures and main tables otherwise retain their displays.

improvement.justification: The added image-transfer and normalized-forecasting experiments provide useful checks of FAN's generalization and dependence on preprocessing, including mixed outcomes. Correcting Figure 2 also improves consistency with the method definition. These gains are limited by sparse specifications for the new experiments, absent uncertainty estimates and the unresolved normalization citation in Table 5.
